validity.researcher_notes: The row is a real, operating trunk line. A Neftegaz article of November 2020 gives length 1,780 km and diameter 1,420 mm, matching the sheet. The Gazprom Transgaz Ekaterinburg notice of April 2021 that is already on the sheet as a Status ref is about the Urengoy-Chelyabinsk pipeline, not this one. A 2015 staff paper gives 1,220 mm for the Tavda crossing. The commissioning year 1978 was not found in the cited Chronicle.

verifications.note: A Neftegaz article of 6 November 2020 (read as an archive copy) reports that Gazprom Transgaz Surgut finished a repair of km 700 to 728 of the first string of the Komsomolskoye-Surgut-Chelyabinsk gas pipeline. This shows the line in service in November 2020. No newer dated citation was opened.

The page does not use the full sheet name and gives no month. Medium because the name match is partial. An earlier note said the chronicle does not list this; that was wrong.

verifications.note: The Neftegaz article of 6 November 2020 says Gazprom Transgaz Surgut carries out the repair on its Surgut linear production department. The Gazprom Transgaz Surgut notice on protection zones for its Purpe department names this pipeline among the lines it services. Both pages name Gazprom Transgaz Surgut, so Operator is staged as that company in the ownership team's style. Other Gazprom subsidiaries service the Ekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk parts, so this is the operator of the Surgut section named in the pages.
